subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Playground Equity: Where Kids Play Matters
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Playground Equity: Where Kids Play Matters.

hook.text: In some US cities, playgrounds in wealthy areas cost $1 million while poor areas get rubber mats and a slide.

buildup.text: Play is how children develop motor skills, social intelligence, and resilience. Access is developmental equity.

discovery.text: Adventure playgrounds — with loose materials, mud, and tools — let kids take risks. They're rare in America.

twist.text: Liability fears killed adventure playgrounds in the US. Europe kept them and child injury rates are actually lower.

climax.text: New York's Imagination Playground uses movable blue foam blocks. Kids design their own space every day.

punchline.text: A rich kid gets a climbing wall. A poor kid gets asphalt. Play isn't equal.

quiz.question: Why did adventure playgrounds decline in the US?
options: Children preferred digital entertainment over outdoor play
Liability fears led to their removal despite lower injury rates elsewhere
Construction costs were too high for most city budgets
